::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

    readRDS(file.path(tcga_dir, "data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem_wide.rds"))

    column_to_rownames("Hugo_Symbol") %>%
```

:::



We'll need to convert the human gene names into mouse gene names to match with the signatures. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mouse_human_genes <- readRDS(here("data",  "mouse_human_genes.rds"))
human_mouse_key <- set_names(mouse_human_genes$MGI.symbol, mouse_human_genes$HGNC.symbol)

new_genes <- human_mouse_key[rownames(tcga_mtx)]
new_genes_filtered <- new_genes[!is.na(new_genes)]

mouse_tcga_mtx <- tcga_mtx[which(!is.na(new_genes)),]
rownames(mouse_tcga_mtx) <- new_genes_filtered
```
:::


## run ssGSEA on SKCM

Now, run ssGSEA on each sample from TCGA SKCM using the myeloid scRNAseq signatures. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
run_gsva <- function(mtx, gs) {
    gsva_out <- gsva(
        mtx,
        gset.idx.list = gs,
        method = "ssgsea",
        kcdf = "Gaussian",
        min.sz = 3
    ) 
    out <- as_tibble(gsva_out, rownames = "gs_name")
    return(out)
}
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gsva_out <- run_or_readRDS(
    file.path(results_dir, "ssGSEA_myeloid_scRNAseq_signatures_20.200.rds"), 
    function() {
        map_dfr(gs_list, ~run_gsva(mouse_tcga_mtx, ..1), .id = "ngenes")
    }
)
gsva_tidy <- gsva_out %>% 
    pivot_longer(cols = 3:ncol(.)) %>% 
    group_by(gs_name, ngenes) %>% 
    mutate(scaled_value = as.vector(scale(value)))
```

## Number of genes included in signature

First, I wanted to examine the effects of changing the number of top differential genes taken to generate the signature. A couple observations: 

* More genes included, higher ssGSEA score. 
* rank order of samples seems consistent upon including 100-200 genes or so. 


::: {.cell fig.asp='1'}

```{.r .cell-code}
gsva_tidy %>% 
    mutate(ngenes = factor(ngenes, levels = sort(as.integer(unique(.$ngenes))))) %>%  
    ggplot() + 
    aes(ngenes, value) + 
    geom_point(size = 0.1) + 
    geom_line(aes(group = name), alpha = 0.1, linewidth = 0.1) + 
    facet_wrap(~gs_name, ncol = 1)
```

Signature using 200 genes seems like a reasonable way to go. 

## Increase in myeloid cell subsets

As expected, with an increase in inflammatory monocytes, we also see an increase in Ccr2 monocytes, MDSC, and M2 macrophages. The highest correlation is between Ccr2 monocytes and inflammatory monocytes. 


::: {.cell}

## Survival in TCGA cohort using inflammatory monocyte to other myeloid score difference

### TCGA SKCM, all

First, we look at how these signatures work against the entire TCGA cohort. 

* Inflamm monocyte vs M2 macs


::: {.cell fig.asp='1'}

```{.r .cell-code}
inflamm_vs_M2_df <- gsva_wide_200 %>% 
    mutate(PATIENT_ID = str_sub(name, end = -4)) %>% 
    filter(PATIENT_ID %in% tcga_data_clinical_patient$PATIENT_ID) %>% 
    mutate(inflamm_vs_M2 = Inflammatory_monocytes_vs_rest - M2_macs_vs_rest) %>% 
    dplyr::select(PATIENT_ID, inflamm_vs_M2) %>% 
    mutate(ratio_high_vs_low = ifelse(inflamm_vs_M2 > median(inflamm_vs_M2), "high", "low"))

os_fit <- survfit(
    Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ ratio_high_vs_low,
    data = tcga_data_clinical_patient %>%
        mutate(OS_STATUS = as.integer(str_extract(OS_STATUS, "."))) %>%
        left_join(inflamm_vs_M2_df, by = "PATIENT_ID")
)
gg <- ggsurvplot(
    os_fit,
    ncensor.plot = FALSE,
    pval = TRUE,
    conf.int = FALSE,
    risk.table = TRUE,
    risk.table.col = "strata",
    linetype = "strata",
    pval.coord = c(5, 0.1)
)
gg
```

# Survival in other cancer types (2018 TCGA Pan can)

Downloaded the TCGA data from cBioPortal FYI. Just went to this URL (https://www.cbioportal.org/datasets) and searched for PanCancer. 

Defining some helper functions to handle the data. Also note there are some key processing choices here, like using the Hugo Symbol instead of the Entrez Gene ID, which could make a difference in results.  


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
read_in_TCGA <- function(subdir) {
    data_clinical_patient <-
        read_tsv(file.path(subdir, "data_clinical_patient.txt"), 
                 skip = 4)
    tpm_mtx <- read_tsv(file.path(subdir, "data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem_zscores_ref_all_samples.txt")) %>% 
        dplyr::select(-Entrez_Gene_Id) %>% 
        drop_na(Hugo_Symbol) %>% 
        {.[!duplicated(.$Hugo_Symbol),]} %>% 
        column_to_rownames("Hugo_Symbol") %>%
        as.matrix()
    
    new_genes <- human_mouse_key[rownames(tpm_mtx)]
    new_genes_filtered <- new_genes[!is.na(new_genes)]
    mouse_tpm_mtx <- tpm_mtx[which(!is.na(new_genes)),]
    rownames(mouse_tpm_mtx) <- new_genes_filtered
    
    return(list(
        data_clinical_patient = data_clinical_patient, 
        tpm_mtx = tpm_mtx, 
        mouse_tpm_mtx = mouse_tpm_mtx
    ))
}
```
